headline: SPYDR is your autonomous red team.
summary: A sanitized replay of a real black-box investigation. Sensitive reproduction details are withheld for responsible disclosure.

timeline.label: Recon
timeline.title: Map the product from the outside
timeline.detail: The agent mapped self-service workflows, public documentation, agent gateways, sandbox boundaries, and observable control-plane behavior.

timeline.label: Model
timeline.title: Find where authority changes
timeline.detail: It separated what happened inside a disposable agent sandbox from actions performed by services outside that sandbox.

timeline.label: Hypothesize
timeline.title: Ask what the product trusts
timeline.detail: Specialist workers proposed competing explanations for an attacker-controlled destination being used by a server-side gateway.

timeline.label: Probe
timeline.title: Run the smallest discriminating test
timeline.detail: An owned callback captured only source, method, and header names. A negative control distinguished gateway behavior from ordinary sandbox egress.

timeline.label: Prove
timeline.title: Show the runtime boundary
timeline.detail: The evidence confirmed that a Runloop service made the request outside the agent sandbox.

timeline.label: Repair
timeline.title: Cut the weakest edge
timeline.detail: SPYDR proposed destination validation, private-address blocking, redirect revalidation, and a regression matrix for the gateway boundary.

proof.confirmed: The request was made by a Runloop-side service outside the disposable agent sandbox.
proof.next: Block unsafe destinations after DNS resolution and revalidate every redirect hop.
